title: Slice-lane mediation for asymmetric canary degradations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Over the last two months we have observed asymmetric degradations where a new model variant in a canary slice shows lower QA pass rates and higher hallucination metrics only for Dedicated and Private deployments while Hosted slices remain nominal. Several customers escalated (INC-2026-031) citing regressions after scheduled rollouts. Hypothesis: differences in KV cache warmup, quantization variant selection, and per-node kernel scheduling cause drift between planes leading to stateful inference artifacts for long-context flows.

Goal: Create a reproducible mediation and rollback choreography that coordinates across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes to: 1) rapidly contain customer impact, 2) reconcile KV cache and stateful artifacts, 3) perform tenant-scoped rollback or surgical mitigation, and 4) provide a clear customer liaison pathway. This ticket owns the operational playbook, automation hooks, and initial pilot run with two impacted customers (tenant-237, tenant-502).
acceptance_criteria: A runbook exists that enumerates step-by-step containment for asymmetric canary degradations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
Automated tenant-quarantine API implemented to split traffic away from canary variant for a given tenant across planes
KV cache reconciliation checklist and automated rehydrate job (safe-mode) validated in a staging slice
Rollback choreography tested end-to-end in lab with synthetic traffic and produces no >2x latency regression
Customer-facing communication templates prepared and approved by Support and Legal
Post-incident dashboard aggregated: per-tenant hallucination rate, latency P95, token cost delta, and KV-staleness signal
notes: 2026-03-01: Triage meeting — agreed scope across SRE, Runtime, Control Plane, and Support. Diego volunteered to lead implementation and field liaison.

2026-03-02: Initial diagnostic — reproducer built for tenant-237: long-context chat with system prompt + retrieval leading to token duplication when using int8-variant on host type b. Suspected stale KV behavior when switching kernels.

2026-03-03: Decision: implement a tenant-scoped quarantine that routes traffic to a pinned stable model version and disables cross-tenant prefix caching for affected tenants. Trade-offs: slightly higher token cost vs immediate quality improvement. Approved by PM (Lydia Park).

2026-03-04: Reviewed control plane changes with Security; SSO token rotation not required. Identified need for an explicit audit log entry for every quarantine action for Private/VPC customers. Added to PR-7321.
2026-03-05: SRE implemented synthetic rehydrate job in staging. Early results show reduced duplicate token rate from 3.8% -> 0.2% for reproducer flows after KV flush + warmup.
steps: Step 0: Notify stakeholders via #inc-operator, page on-call SRE and runtime oncall
Step 1: Run diagnostic script (scripts/rollouts/kv-staleness-check.sh) against tenant slice to collect KV hit/miss, kernel-version, and quantization profile
Step 2: Invoke tenant-quarantine API to split 100% of traffic off canary variant for affected tenant(s) and pin to last known-good model version
Step 3: Trigger KV safe-mode rehydrate job: flush prefix cache + synthetic warmup traffic to refill stable prefix entries
Step 4: Monitor dashboards for 30 minutes: hallucination rate, P95 latency, token cost delta; if metrics improve, plan controlled rollout re-intro with 1% increments

Step 5: If metrics do not improve in 60 minutes, perform cross-plane coordinated rollback (control plane orchestrates model pinning in Dedicated and applies private-agent patch for on-prem) and notify customer success lead
Step 6: After containment, collect debug bundle and open postmortem draft; schedule customer readout within 48 hours
customer_communication: Template A (initial): We’re aware of increased error/quality regressions for your instance during the recent model rollout. We’ve initiated a tenant-scoped mitigation that pins to a stable model and are running reconciliations. Expected time to resolution: 1–3 hours. — Support
Template B (post-action): We rolled back the canary variant for your tenant and rehydrated model state. We will share a technical summary and next steps within 48 hours. — Field Engineering
followups: Add a KV-staleness alert (derived metric) to per-tenant dashboards (ENG-305210)
Add test harness scenario in runtime-integration-suite that simulates kernel-switch during active KV session (ENG-305211)
Run postmortem and schedule a cross-team retro with Support/Legal/Product within 7 days
review_feedback: PM feedback (Lydia Park): include customer SLA impact window and alternative credit/remediation offers
Design feedback (Marco Ivers): add UX flags in Console to visualize per-tenant quarantine state
SRE feedback (Priya Rao): make synthetic rehydrate job idempotent and safe for edge/private deployments
